                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:538" />17 And their word will eat as doth <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>gangrene.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> a can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ker <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> it is, <ns0:hi>And their word will have pasture,</ns0:hi> [or place to feed upon] as a <ns0:hi>Gangrene,</ns0:hi> we have ill translated the word a <ns0:hi>Cancer,</ns0:hi> for it signifieth a <ns0:hi>Gangrene</ns0:hi>; both our <ns0:hi>English</ns0:hi> word <ns0:hi>Gan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />grene,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Latin</ns0:hi> word or derived from the <ns0:hi>Greek.</ns0:hi> There is a great difference between a <ns0:hi>Cancer</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Gangrene,</ns0:hi> in the cau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses of those two Diseases, and the nature of them, and the time in which they destroy the body of a man; only they both agree in their infecting the parts contiguous, the <ns0:hi>Cancer</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ating them, the <ns0:hi>Gangrene</ns0:hi> mortifying them, and for this, the words of erroneous persons are here compared to this Disease, because either of them will have something to feed upon; (so <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> signifieth, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 10.9.) most errours in matters of Faith are contagious and infectious; the reason is, because ordinari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly an error is broached by some, and entertained by others in satisfaction to some Lust, as favouring some evil desire and in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />clination of our minds, and so naturally pleaseth those who have the same evil propensions.</ns0:note>, of whom is Hymeneus and Philetus <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Of <ns0:hi>Hymeneus</ns0:hi> we read before, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.20. there he is joyned with <ns0:hi>Alexander,</ns0:hi> but not of <ns0:hi>Philetus,</ns0:hi> nor do we find him further mentioned in Holy Writ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Who <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Tim. 6.21.</ns0:note> concerning the truth have erred <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">These two he saith had already erred as to the Doctrine of Faith, giving heed to profane and vain bablings.</ns0:note>, saying that the resurrection is past already <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Their par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticular Error was in the business of the <ns0:hi>Resurrection,</ns0:hi> which they said was past. That <ns0:hi>there shall be no Resurrection,</ns0:hi> is a very plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing Doctrine to men that have lived sensual lives, those whose lives have been nothing but eating and drinking, do very un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />willingly think of dying, but seeing they cannot avoid that, they would gladly there should be no Resurrection. So that it was no wonder if such an Error as this did spread and mortifie like a <ns0:hi>Gangrene.</ns0:hi> Upon what pretence these men denied the Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection, we are neither told in Holy Writ, nor with any cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainty by any other Authors. Some say, that they held that it was past in the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of Christ,</ns0:hi> and those mentioned, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 27.52. Others think they confounded the <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Regeneration,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Glorification,</ns0:hi> which they allowed only as to the Souls of Believers. Others say they maintained no other <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi> than <ns0:hi>what men have in the Procreation of Children.</ns0:hi> O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers, that they denied any Resurrection but that in <ns0:hi>Baptisme.</ns0:hi> The Resurrection of the Body was denied by the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> by these in <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> time, and afterwards by those that fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed, <ns0:hi>Marcion, Basilides, Valentinus</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Apelles,</ns0:hi> and others. Some in our times also have troden in their steps, and are still treading (unless they think God will be more kind to those in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />finite numbers of Heathens in the Country of the Great <ns0:hi>Mogul</ns0:hi> than to <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi>; for as to them, they tell us they cannot believe any such thing). Two sorts of men have been guilty of this; 1. The Philosophers of the World that think they must be able with their Reason to span all Articles of Faith. 2. Men of sensual and sottish lives, who having lived like beasts are wil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling to believe they shall also die like brutes.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Those who are tainted with this Error do both themselves deny the <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> divers principal Articles of which depend upon it. Such as the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of Christ,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15. and <ns0:hi>Eternal Life, &c.</ns0:hi> and also subvert <ns0:hi>the faith</ns0:hi> of others; for whoso can perswade another that there shall be no Resurrection, makes him an infidel. Such Hereticks therefore were never indured to keep any Station in the Christian Church. It being always judged reasonable, that those who were turned Infidels, should be turned out of the flock of Christ to their proper Herd.</ns0:note>, and overthrow the faith of some <ns0:hi>s.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Nevertheless, the foundation of God <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Notwithstanding that these two men (possibly of some note in the Church of <ns0:hi>Ephesus</ns0:hi>) have fallen from the Faith, and have been ill instruments to subvert the Faith of others, yet God hath a number in the World, who are built upon the Rock Christ Jesus, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 7.25. these are founded surely,</ns0:note> standeth <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>steady.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> sure, having this seal; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 10.14. see Num. 16.5.</ns0:note> The Lord knoweth them that are his <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Seal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, and confirmed in their State by the Eternal Decree and Counsel of God, who hath foreknown his Elect, both as to their number and perseverance, but God hath from Eternity known who are his, and therefore such as truly are so, must be kept through Faith by his Power to Salvation, and it is not possible that these should be totally and finally deceived.</ns0:note>, and, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry one that nameth the name of the Lord must depart from the Tents of wicked men, who have made shipwrack both of Faith, and a good Conscience; therefore let not the Apostacy of these men be a Temptation to thee to think that the Church of God may or shall <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>ail; that cannot be, there can be no more lost than the sons of Perdition; such as God never knew as his though they put on a mark of Christianity and Godliness, and deceived many. Those who have Gods Seal upon them, and are of his Foundation, shall stand and keep themselves from those damnable Errors. Onely to let us know that neither the certainty of Gods Decree or Promise, doth excuse our indea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vours and using means for obtaining the thing decreed or pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised; the Apostle puts the Verb in the Imperative Mood, <ns0:hi>Let him depart, &c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold, and of silver, but also of wood, and of earth <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Look as it is in a great house, there are several Vessels, made of several materials, and for several ends, and uses. Some are made of gold, some of Silver, some of Wood, some of Earth.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 9.21.</ns0:note> and some to honour, and some to dishonour <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Some made and bought for more Noble and Honour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />able uses, others for more vile, base, and dishonourable uses: so it is in the Church of God, which is large, and like a great house. In it are many Members; some have obtained like precious Faith with us, who are as Gold tried in the fire, or like silver purified seven times, by the Word of God, and his Spirit sitting as a Refiner upon their Hearts. But all they are not Gold or Silver who glister in an outward profession; some of them have earthy, wooden Souls, savouring onely sensual things, having nothing of precious Faith in them, and are not yet purged from their filthiness, wanting all truth of Grace, or sincerity of Love: Some whose work is to honour God, being created to good Works, and whose reward will be to be hon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />oured and glorified by him: Others who by their Apostacy from their Faith, and profession, and by their wicked lives will dishonour him, and will be Eternally rejected by him as Reprobate Silver, and sons of Perdition.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="22">22 Flee also youthful lusts <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By youthful Lusts he means such sinful desires, propensi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, and inclinations of Mind as are most incident to youth, whether they be lusts of the <ns0:hi>flesh,</ns0:hi> or spiritual Lusts, such as are the Vices of the Mind, Ambition, Ostentation, Pride, Vain<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />glory, Contempt of others, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>: but <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Tim. 6.11.</ns0:note> follow righteousness <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Follow Justice, or Inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cency, which wrongeth none, but rendereth to every one his due, or the righteousness of an holy life.</ns0:note>, faith <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> which teach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth a Soul to receive Divine Revelations steadily, without per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verse disputings.</ns0:note>, charity <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Charity,</ns0:hi> which is kind, <ns0:hi>envieth not, vaunteth not it self, is not puffed up, doth not behave it self unseemly, seeketh not her own,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 13.4, 5, 6.</ns0:note>, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">An Union not with men of corrupt Minds and Practices, but with all such as serve and wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship God purely and sincerely.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">It is a precept or caution of the same nature with those, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.4. and 4: 7. and <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 16. of this Chapter. The repetition of this precept of the Apostle four times in these two short Epistles, lets us know how important a thing he judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed it, that Ministers of the Gospel should not spend their times in their Discourses to their Congregations, in things that tend nothing to the building up of their hearers in Faith or Holi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, being either old Wives Fables, like the stories in the <ns0:hi>Popish Legends,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Apochryphal stories</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Bell</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Dragon, Tobit</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Dog,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Swallows dunging in his Eye, &c.</ns0:hi> or sifting out <ns0:hi>Genealogies,</ns0:hi> or vain and impertinent discourses or idle fruitless questions which tend not to <ns0:hi>edifying,</ns0:hi> but to satisfie curiosity, and increase strife and ungodliness, which kind of Preaching the Apostle also had defamed, 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.4. as the issue of Pride, and Ignorance, and Dotage, and here he calls such questions <ns0:hi>unlearned</ns0:hi> in the same sense because impertinent to the end of Preaching. The Vanity of Humane Nature and their non-subjection to the Will of God appeareth much in this, that notwithstanding the unreasonableness of such Preachings, and the direct opposition of it to the so often repeated pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cepts of the Apostle, and to <ns0:hi>Titus, chap.</ns0:hi> 3.9. and <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> propo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing of his own Example to the contrary, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.1, 2, 3, 4. yet for many years in the times of <ns0:hi>Popery</ns0:hi> the People were fed with little besides these Husks, and too many yet, either out of <ns0:hi>Pride,</ns0:hi> to shew their parts and reading, or ignorance of the misteries of Godliness, and the true end of preaching, or <ns0:hi>dotage</ns0:hi> about unprofitable speculations and niceties can find little bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter food than these Husks for poor peoples Souls.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:538" />25 In <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gal. 6.1.</ns0:note> meekness instructing those that op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose themselves <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Without Passion, better informing such as have suckt in an error, nor reviling them, but gently instructing them, and la<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bouring to convince them of their mistake; for all those who for a time may oppose the Truth, are not such as never repent, nor do it out of malice, or hatred, they may do it out of igno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rance, and weakness.</ns0:note>; if <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 8.22.</ns0:note> God peradventure will give them repentance, to the acknowledging of the truth <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">and God may give them a power, and an heart to repent, and to acknowledge that truth which they at present oppose, and although this must be Gods work, yet he doth it by Ministers as his means, and instruments, who are to use probable means in order to it, such are not railing and reviling, but meek instructions, and a kind and gentle behaviour to them.
